subject: general
question: In May 2025, which organization released the Global Report on Food Crises, highlighting rising hunger due to conflict and climate extremes?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Global Network Against Food Crises**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Global Network Against Food Crises** is an international alliance founded in 2016 by the **European Union (EU), Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), and World Food Programme (WFP).**
 
• It aims to tackle food crises through coordinated humanitarian and development action, addressing the root causes of hunger and promoting food security worldwide.
 
• The **Global Report on Food Crises** is its flagship annual publication, which provides critical insights into the state of global food insecurity and its drivers, such as **conflict, climate extremes, and economic shocks.**
 
• The report for **May 2025** highlights a significant rise in hunger globally, attributing the alarming trend primarily to factors like **armed conflicts** and worsening **climate-related disasters.**
 
• The organization collaborates with multiple stakeholders, including governments, international agencies, and NGOs, to implement solutions and strategies that address both immediate needs and long-term stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO):**

 
 
• The **FAO** is a specialized agency of the United Nations that leads international efforts to defeat hunger.
 
• Established in **1945**, it focuses on improving agricultural productivity, ensuring food security, and promoting sustainable development in rural areas.
 
• Its work includes conducting research, publishing reports, and providing policy recommendations to governments and stakeholders.
 
 
 
• **World Bank:**
 
 
• The **World Bank** is an international financial institution established in **1944** to provide loans and grants to countries for development projects.
 
• Although it addresses poverty and economic development, its focus is broader than food crises, encompassing areas like education, infrastructure, and healthcare.
 
• It contributes to food security indirectly by funding projects aimed at agricultural innovation and rural development.
 
 
 
• **UN Environment Programme (UNEP):**
 
 
• The **UNEP** was founded in **1972** and focuses on the global environment, addressing issues such as climate change, biodiversity loss, and pollution.
 
• While it does not directly produce food-related reports, it highlights the environmental factors that impact agriculture and food security.
 
• UNEP emphasizes climate mitigation and adaptation to ensure sustainable ecosystems for food production.
 
 
 
• **Global Network Against Food Crises:**
 
 
• The network operates as a collaborative platform, bringing together humanitarian and development agencies to address food crises.
 
• It emphasizes data-driven decision-making, publishing the **Global Report on Food Crises** annually to guide policy interventions.
 
• Through partnerships, the network aims to reduce the number of people experiencing acute food insecurity and prevent future crises.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Drivers of Food Crises:**

 
 
• **Conflict:** Armed conflicts disrupt agricultural production, trade, and livelihoods, leading to food shortages and inflation.
 
• **Climate Extremes:** Events like droughts, floods, and hurricanes severely impact food production and availability.
 
• **Economic Shocks:** Inflation, unemployment, and reduced income levels exacerbate food insecurity, particularly in vulnerable populations.
 
 
 
• **Global Hunger Statistics:**
 
 
• As of **2025**, over **250 million people** globally are experiencing acute food insecurity due to the mentioned drivers.
 
• The regions most affected include **Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and parts of the Middle East.**
 
• Women and children are disproportionately impacted, with long-term effects on health and development.
 
 
 
• **Collaborative Efforts:**
 
 
• Organizations like **FAO, WFP, and UNEP** work together to provide short-term relief and promote sustainable solutions.
 
• Innovative approaches include climate-resilient agriculture, disaster risk reduction, and improved food distribution systems.
